evaluations.result: The data contains 15 EQ-TIPS papers from 2023 to 2026: 10 measurement evaluations, three methods studies, one framework study, and one instrument-development study.
evaluations.cause: Titles, instrument uses, study families, findings, and publication dates support a coherent summary.

evaluations.result: Five EQ-HWB adaptation papers cover Argentinian Spanish, Simplified Chinese, Italian, German, and English or multinational development work.
evaluations.cause: Translation purpose, publication, and administration-language data identify the adaptations.

evaluations.result: A ten-paper ranking is available; the 2012 EQ-5D-5L interim-scoring paper ranks first with 2,231 OpenAlex citations.
evaluations.cause: Valuation purposes and dated OpenAlex citation counts support the ranking.

evaluations.result: A crosswalk predicts scores between systems; a native value set directly values states in its target system. The 2012 interim-scoring paper and the 2017 England and China value-set papers are key examples.
evaluations.cause: Separate mapping purposes and value-set study families prevent the two products from being merged.

evaluations.result: A reliable institution ranking is not available.
evaluations.cause: Affiliations are unnormalized author source text, and projects have no host-institution relation.

evaluations.result: Student-grant candidates and their principal investigators can be listed, but supervisors and host institutions cannot be identified safely.
evaluations.cause: The data has only a principal-investigator project role and no supervisor or project-institution relation.

evaluations.result: cTTO appears most often in funded valuation-related work, followed by DCE, descriptive statistics, quota sampling, and lead-time TTO.
evaluations.cause: Accepted project-output links, valuation purposes, and canonical current-study methods support the counts.

evaluations.result: The data contains 66 EQ-5D-Y-5L papers, led by 39 measurement evaluations and 11 methods studies.
evaluations.cause: Publication, study-family, and instrument-use data support a dated research summary.

evaluations.result: The open-access introductory set includes the 2021 domain-identification paper and the 2022 patient and public involvement paper.
evaluations.cause: Titles, development purposes, and open-access flags support the selection.

evaluations.result: From 2024 through 2026, measurement-property evaluation shows the largest increase, followed by content-validity evaluation and instrument development.
evaluations.cause: Controlled research purposes and publication years support a three-year comparison.

evaluations.result: A corpus timeline can show first appearances of EQ-5D-3L in 2005, EQ-5D-5L and EQ-5D-Y in 2010, and later instrument variants and products.
evaluations.cause: Dated publications, canonical instrument identities, research products, and product states support milestones.

evaluations.result: No institution was supplied.
evaluations.cause: The placeholder “institution X” must be replaced with a name.

evaluations.result: The data can list observed native EQ-5D-5L value sets, but it cannot safely identify every country that lacks one.
evaluations.cause: Missing corpus evidence is not evidence that a national value set does not exist.

evaluations.result: The leading systematic review is “Psychometric properties of the EQ-5D-5L,” with 940 OpenAlex citations; the 3L-versus-5L review follows with 375.
evaluations.cause: Review metadata, titles, and dated citation counts support the ranking.

evaluations.result: Youth-instrument papers appear most often in Value in Health, Pharmacoeconomics, Quality of Life Research, and Health and Quality of Life Outcomes.
evaluations.cause: Current youth-instrument uses and publication journals support the counts.

evaluations.result: A title-and-ID screen finds 32 possible student projects, of which 11 have linked publications and 249 extracted findings.
evaluations.cause: Student-grant status is not a controlled project type, so the candidate set depends on text rules.

evaluations.result: A bounded starter list can combine highly cited valuation-method papers, major protocols, value-set studies, and recent evidence syntheses.
evaluations.cause: Study purpose, study family, publication date, open access, and citation data support transparent selection rules.

evaluations.result: Of 208 EQ-5D methods papers, 39, or 18.8%, name EuroQol in the funding statement.
evaluations.cause: The measure uses explicit funding-statement text and does not substitute broader support or project-link evidence.

evaluations.result: The annual series starts with one paper in 2004 and reaches 132 in 2025; the evidence base has no publications dated before 2004.
evaluations.cause: Publication years support the series, with a scope warning for the empty 1990–2003 period.

evaluations.result: Member co-author edges can be extracted, but named communities depend on a selected clustering method and resolution.
evaluations.cause: The question does not specify a community algorithm, and no community assignments are stored.

evaluations.result: Of 603 funded-output papers, 319 are open access, for a share of 52.9%; annual values rise from low early levels to about 59% in 2025.
evaluations.cause: Accepted output links, publication years, and open-access flags support the result.

evaluations.result: Funded-linked papers have a mean of 32.4 OpenAlex citations, compared with 144.0 for other corpus papers by resolved researchers.
evaluations.cause: Resolved authors, accepted links, and the dated citation snapshot support the comparison.

evaluations.result: A valid countries-per-paper co-authorship trend is not available.
evaluations.cause: Study countries describe research settings, while author affiliations are unnormalized and do not provide author-country identities.

evaluations.result: Using first accepted authorship as entry, 554 researchers entered from 2024 through 2026: 185 in 2024, 251 in 2025, and 118 in 2026.
evaluations.cause: Resolved author identities and publication years support the corpus-entry measure.

evaluations.result: All 439 links with complete project dates fall in the −1 to +8 year window; this confirms 68.4% of all 642 links, while 203 links remain unclassified.
evaluations.cause: Missing project end dates prevent an exact fraction for all accepted links.

evaluations.result: Thirty publications link to more than one project; the EQ-HWB psychometric survey paper links to six projects, the highest count.
evaluations.cause: Accepted project-output links support the publication-level counts.

evaluations.result: The top decile of 297 principal investigators accounts for 332 of 629 linked outputs, or 52.8%.
evaluations.cause: Resolved principal-investigator roles and accepted output links support the concentration measure.

evaluations.result: Among researchers without an observed membership record, Kim Dalziel has the most papers with observed members, at 27.
evaluations.cause: The result uses absence of observed membership only and does not claim confirmed non-membership.

evaluations.result: The public data cannot return citation components or hubs; the private evidence confirms 4,100 resolved within-corpus citation edges.
evaluations.cause: Paper reference edges are intentionally absent from the serving database.

evaluations.result: Inter-project citation flow is not available in the public data, although private reference evidence contains 1,963 directed project pairs.
evaluations.cause: The serving database has citation totals but no citing-to-cited publication edges.

evaluations.result: Of 1,734 researchers with accepted publication identities, 1,302 have an ORCID, for a share of 75.1%.
evaluations.cause: Accepted author resolution and reviewed person identifiers support the calculation.

evaluations.result: One publication has no abstract, but papers with truncated author lists cannot be identified.
evaluations.cause: Missing abstracts are directly detectable, but no author-list truncation flag is stored.

evaluations.result: Papers per project can be compared for exact working-group strings, but a reliable per-group comparison is incomplete.
evaluations.cause: One project field can contain multiple working-group labels instead of normalized project-group relations.

evaluations.result: The graph has 1,893 person researchers and 125 observed members; it also contains 16 group identities that are excluded from the researcher count.
evaluations.cause: Reviewed person types and observed membership records support the totals.

evaluations.result: OpenAlex topics or fields that cite funded work cannot be ranked.
evaluations.cause: The citation snapshot has counts and yearly totals but no citing-work topic or field data.

evaluations.result: Citation-lag distribution is unavailable in the public data; private evidence has 4,100 resolved edges with a mean lag of 4.22 years.
evaluations.cause: The public release omits the citing-to-cited paper relation needed to calculate lag.

evaluations.result: The data reports 31 identifier-consolidation authorships and identity acceptance statuses, but it cannot list all merged, overridden, or skipped profiles with reasons.
evaluations.cause: Resolution methods and outcomes are stored, but full decision-level audit reasons are not.

evaluations.result: Funded papers cannot be ranked by venue impact.
evaluations.cause: Journal names are present, but journal impact factors or another venue-impact measure are absent.

evaluations.result: No project was supplied.
evaluations.cause: The placeholder “project X” must be replaced with a project ID or title.

evaluations.result: The public data cannot identify value-set products that later corpus papers reference.
evaluations.cause: Value-set products are present, but publication reference edges are absent from the serving database.

evaluations.result: The top recent completed project is project 330-PHD with nine outputs and 79 OpenAlex citations, followed by 304-PHD with seven outputs and 44 citations.
evaluations.cause: Project dates, completion status, accepted outputs, and citations retrieved on 2026-08-27 support the ranking.

evaluations.result: The funnel is 1,024 projects, 400 projects with outputs, 603 distinct output papers, and 17,345 OpenAlex citations.
evaluations.cause: Accepted output links and the dated citation snapshot support each stage.

evaluations.result: Using the earliest project year and including tied first grants, 137 of 297 first-time principal investigators have an output from that first-year grant set.
evaluations.cause: Resolved principal-investigator roles, project start years, and accepted output links support the calculation.

evaluations.result: Distinct resolved co-author edges increase from 9 in the 2000s to 3,155 in the 2010s and 14,033 in the 2020s.
evaluations.cause: Publication dates and resolved co-authorship pairs support decade-level network growth.

evaluations.result: A bounded text screen finds 79 projects linked to 121 studies of children, adolescents, cognitive impairment, or dementia.
evaluations.cause: Population labels are source text, and “under-represented” is not a controlled classification.

evaluations.result: The data identifies 54 bolt-on-related papers, including 31 with bolt-ons in the title; each has an abstract or extracted finding for a short summary.
evaluations.cause: The set is below the row limit, and topical uses plus study evidence support one-line summaries.

evaluations.result: The number of researcher countries in funded publications cannot be calculated reliably.
evaluations.cause: Author affiliations are unnormalized source text and no researcher-country relation exists.

evaluations.result: No DOI was supplied.
evaluations.cause: The placeholder “DOI X” must be replaced with a DOI.

evaluations.result: The excluded share cannot be calculated because all 797 available publications have the include-study disposition.
evaluations.cause: Pure-application exclusions and their member authors are absent from both current databases.

evaluations.result: The private data marks all 642 accepted links as full-text confirmed, but it cannot compare graph-entry routes with structured funder metadata.
evaluations.cause: No explicit publication-entry provenance field distinguishes the two routes.
